text:
maria: heads up — onboarding orpheus-7b-int4 into long-context suite. after ~12k tokens we see divergence from fp16 baseline (repeated phrasing + hallucinations). attaching quick logs. :eyes:
jamie: repro steps? input, quant config, runtime flags?
sasha: which quant scheme did you use — per-channel or per-tensor? and any asymmetric clipping?
maria: per-channel symmetric, clip=0.015, zero-point disabled. runtime: rwin=65536, kv-shard=auto. repro input is a ~14k token concatenation of several legal docs (sanitized). snippet:
```
[INPUT TRUNCATED] ... token_pos ~12112
LAYER 9: kv_index_expected=12112 kv_index_actual=12111
LAYER 10: kv_index_expected=12112 kv_index_actual=12111
ERROR: kv_cache_alignment_mismatch at step 12112
Generation diverges from fp16 at token 12114: "the agreement was" -> fp16 vs int4: "there agreement were"
```
ting: hmm, kv_index off-by-one in multiple layers — that smells like RoPE position scaling/overflow during quantized matmul or an index arithmetic edge. did you enable rotary rescale fallback?
maria: we left runtime defaults (rotary_rescale=true). also saw small shifts in rotary phase params during warmstart.
sasha: try forcing rotary_rescale=false and rerun a short longprefill to ~13k. if drift goes away, it's likely our rescale interpolation interacting badly with int4 kernel rounding.
jamie: started a quick job with rotary_rescale=false + quant_clip=0.02. cmd:
```bash
./runtest --model orpheus-7b-int4 --suite longprefill --max-tokens 14000 --rotary_rescale=false --quant_clip 0.02 --log-level debug
```
jamie: preliminary: no kv_index mismatch up to 13k, text aligned with fp16 for first 350 tokens of divergence window. still running full.
maria: thanks. can you dump kvcache checksums every 1k tokens? i want to diff against fp16 run.
jamie: added checksums. sample:
```
ksum_fp16_layer9@12000=0x9a3f12b4
ksum_int4_layer9@12000=0x9a3f12b4
ksum_fp16_layer9@12112=0x8b12ff00
ksum_int4_layer9@12112=0x8b12feff  # off by 1
```
sasha: off-by-one checksum delta confirms K/V write index rounding. i think the int4 matmul fused kernel increments the write pointer after packing in a different order when rotary rescales trigger a split path.
maria: interesting. regression: fp16 baseline used one codepath; int4 uses fused_kv_pack which does early commit on partial blocks.
ting: workaround: bump kvcache allocation to align block sizes (pad to 512 token blocks) or force non-fused pack for int4 for now. which is cheaper?
jamie: quick cost: forcing non-fused pack increases CPU overhead but tests show stable correctness. padding to 512 increases memory by ~3% and also stable. i'll try padding first.
maria: test results with padding=512: no mismatch, generation aligned through full 14k. we should still root-cause.
sasha: next step: add micro-bench for fused_kv_pack ordering w/ rotary_rescale toggles and int4 rounding modes. i'll own that.
maria: opened a short-lived incident for tracking: inc-2026-0422. triage-bot: created inc-2026-0422: "orpheus-7b-int4 kv-cache hysteresis during longprefill"
triage-bot: severity: S3, owner: eng-ml-oncall
jamie: also ran quant variant per-tensor (was per-channel originally) — per-tensor had worse drift earlier (diverged earlier at ~9k). per-channel is better but still vulnerable when rescale=true.
ting: summary actionable items:
- add longprefill regression test (14k) to onboarding pipeline for any int4 model (maria)
- add fused_kv_pack unit test that verifies write-order invariants under rotary_rescale (sasha)
- temporarily set default rotary_rescale=false for int4 on Dedicated until patch (ops: jamie)
- add CI job with padding=512 to catch regression (devex)
maria: i'll draft the PR for pipeline test + note in model onboarding checklist to run both per-channel and per-tensor quant configs.
jamie: opened draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4021 — includes kvcache-checksum artifact and job config.
sasha: i'll attach microbench results and a minimal repro (small input that triggers same off-by-one after a few repeated segments) to the PR.
maria: tl;dr — root cause likely interaction between fused int4 packing and rotary_rescale codepath causing write-order non-determinism. mitigation: padding or disabling rescale until fused pack ordering fixed. plan to backport fix to int4 kernels and add regression tests. :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: scheduled config change (rotary_rescale=false for int4) to roll out to staging at 2026-04-23T03:00:00Z, prod tentative 2026-04-24T03:00:00Z (after postmortem).
jamie: can someone add a short note to onboarding playbook? i updated PR description but need doc edit.
maria: will do. thanks all.
